broker.name: STARTRADER
broker.tagline: A conduct licence was not confirmed on the pages that loaded. Rules depend on where you live. Advertised leverage: Up to 1:1000.
broker.about: The STARTRADER pages checked on 11 October 2026 do not state a founding year or one headquarters. Account names on its site include Standard, ECN, and Prime ECN. Platforms named there include MetaTrader 4, MetaTrader 5, Web Trader, Mobile app, STAR Copy, and Pro-Link. Those pages do not confirm a conduct licence we could list with a country and a regulator name. Minimum deposit is not a single number on the pages that loaded. The highest leverage figure taken from those pages is Up to 1:1000. Leverage increases losses as well as gains.
broker.regulators_note: The company behind an account depends on where you live. No regulator entry is listed because the pages that loaded did not confirm one.

broker.leverage_note: Leverage increases losses as well as gains, and you can lose more than you deposit. The highest figure on this card is the highest number this broker advertises. It is not the cap on every account. The cap depends on the company, the product and where you live.

other_fees.label: Minimum deposit
other_fees.note: The accounts page does not state STARTRADER's own minimum deposit. Its FAQ talks about minimum deposits at brokers in general ($5 to $10, or $100 or more) and is not a STARTRADER figure. STAR Copy says copiers can start with USD 50, and a later answer says 50 in any currency. Becoming a STAR Master requires a single deposit of at least USD 500. Those are copy-trading thresholds, not a firm-wide account minimum.

_notes.fetch_notes: Homepage, accounts and STAR Copy pages fetched. Legal-documents and webterminal fetches did not return the licence footer. Search excerpts of those URLs quoted Seychelles FSA SD049, Mauritius FSC GB24203371 and South Africa FSCA 52464, plus ASIC AFSL 421210 and UAE CMA 20200000241 on a knowledge-article excerpt. A direct fetch of that knowledge article did not include those licence lines, so licence numbers, entities and countries are left null. The homepage fetch listed CMA, FSCA, FSA and FSC under a heading that said 5 regulations. A later search excerpt of the homepage also inserted ASIC. Only the four names returned by the homepage fetch are stored. Homepage also says Financial Commission compensation up to 20,000 euros for eligible claims, and Lloyd's coverage up to US$30,000,000. No founding year, headquarters or bonus code was on the pages that rendered.
